description: Paper classification into three tiers for the quantum finance research project. A paper can belong to multiple tiers and multiple groups within each tier.

tier-1.name: General & Contextual
tier-1.description: Papers that provide landscape coverage, theoretical foundations, or contextual framing for quantum computing in finance. Reviews, surveys, tutorials, analytical/theoretical contributions, benchmarking studies, and QC or computational finance foundations.

qc-industry.description: Quantum computing industry landscape, hardware roadmaps, general QC surveys, error mitigation, noise analysis

computational-finance.description: Computational/quantitative finance overviews, classical methods landscape, mathematical finance foundations

qc-in-finance-overview.description: Quantum computing in finance surveys, tutorials, landscape papers, roadmaps, benchmarking across methods, advantage assessments, analytical proofs of quantum speedup

tier-1.classification_guidance: Classify here if ANY of: (1) review/survey/tutorial/position paper; (2) QC industry, hardware, or quantum advantage across multiple domains; (3) evaluation_type=conceptual_only; (4) evaluation_type=analytical — theoretical proofs, complexity analyses, analytical derivations (foundational theory). Do NOT classify merely because a paper compares its method against a classical baseline — that is standard Tier 2+3. Tier 1 is for papers whose contribution IS the overview, theory, or framing.

tier-2.name: Problem-Specific
tier-2.description: Papers focused on a specific financial problem domain. May propose, adapt, or evaluate quantum approaches for that problem.
tier-2.classification_guidance: Classify here if the paper's primary contribution is framed around a specific financial problem (portfolio optimization, derivatives pricing, risk management, etc.), regardless of whether it includes an experiment. Use unified_taxonomy.json topic_tags as groups. A paper can belong to multiple Tier 2 groups if it addresses multiple problems.

tier-3.name: Algorithm & Experiment
tier-3.description: Papers that implement and test quantum algorithms applied to finance problems. Contains quantitative results from simulation or real hardware.
tier-3.classification_guidance: Classify here if the paper runs experiments (simulation or real QPU) and reports quantitative results for a finance application. Use unified_taxonomy.json methodology_tags as groups. A paper testing QAOA for portfolio optimization would also appear in Tier 2 (portfolio-optimization) and Tier 3 (qaoa). Papers that only provide theoretical proofs without quantitative evaluation belong in Tier 2 only.

classification_review.workflow: LLM classifies → writes tier_classification.csv with review_status='draft_llm' → human reviews and changes to 'approved' or 'rejected' → only approved papers are pushed to Zotero
